title: Modals of deduction and speculation
titleVi: Động từ khuyết thiếu: suy đoán
summary: Suy luận theo mức độ chắc chắn với must, can't, may, might, could — kỹ năng hedge bắt buộc trong Task 2.
whyItMatters: Bài viết band 7.5+ không khẳng định tuyệt đối khi chưa đủ bằng chứng. `Must`, `might`, `could` cho phép bạn thể hiện mức độ tin cậy khác nhau trong cùng một câu, và `can't` là cách phủ định suy đoán mà nhiều thí sinh Việt Nam dùng sai thành `mustn't`.

sections.heading: must and can't: confident deduction
body: **must + base verb** means the evidence makes you certain something is true: *You must be tired after such a long flight.*
**can't + base verb** means the evidence makes you certain something is impossible: *You can't be hungry — you ate twenty minutes ago.*
Note the asymmetry: there is no *mustn't* for deduction. To deny a deduction, use **can't** (or **couldn't**).

examples.right: The lights are on, so she must be at home.
He can't be serious about resigning.
examples.wrong: He mustn't be serious about resigning.
examples.note: Phủ định suy đoán dùng **can't**, không dùng **mustn't**.

examples.right: They must have left early — the office is empty.
examples.note: Deduction about the past uses **must have + V3**.

sections.heading: may, might and could: degrees of possibility
body: **may**, **might** and **could** all mark possibility, with **might** and **could** slightly less certain than **may** in many contexts.
The negative of a possibility is **may not / might not** (= perhaps not). This is very different from **can't** (= definitely not).
*It may rain tomorrow* means rain is possible; *It can't rain tomorrow* means it is impossible.
**May** is the most formal of the three and appears often in academic writing: *This may explain the discrepancy in the data.*

examples.right: The delay may be caused by the new customs procedure.
She might not accept the offer — the salary is lower than expected.
This approach could reduce costs by 15%.

sections.heading: Structures after the modal
body: Deduction modals combine with different verb forms to place the speculation in time: **modal + be** (state now), **modal + be + -ing** (activity now), **modal + base verb** (future or general), **modal + have + V3** (past).
So: *She must be at work* (now, state) / *She must be working* (now, activity) / *She must have left* (past).
The participle after **have** is always V3: *must have gone*, never *must have went*.

rows: It may take longer than planned.
It might work; it could fail.

sections.heading: may be, maybe and might in unreal situations
body: **maybe** is one word and means *perhaps*; **may be** is a modal + verb. Compare *Maybe the report is late* with *The report may be late.*
In conditional or unreal contexts, use **might**, not **may**: *If they paid teachers better, more graduates might enter the profession.*
**Might as well** means there is no better alternative: *The bus is delayed, so we might as well walk.*

examples.wrong: May be the figures are wrong.
examples.note: Câu mở đầu bằng trạng từ cần **maybe** (một từ).

examples.right: If funding increased, more rural clinics might stay open.
The venue is closed, so we might as well cancel.

sections.heading: Hedging in IELTS Task 2
body: Strong claims without evidence lower your score in Task Response and can sound naive. Replace flat assertions with a modal of possibility.
Instead of *Advertising destroys consumer choice*, write *Advertising may distort consumer choice, particularly among younger buyers.*
Combine a modal with a qualifying phrase (*in some cases*, *to a certain extent*, *particularly among*) to produce the balanced register examiners reward at band 7.5 and above.

examples.right: Advertising may distort consumer choice, particularly among younger buyers.
Remote work could reduce urban congestion, although the effect might be limited.
examples.note: Two hedges in one balanced sentence.

examples.right: The policy can't be the only cause of the decline.
examples.wrong: The policy mustn't be the only cause of the decline.

commonMistakes.wrong: He mustn't be at home — all the lights are off.
commonMistakes.right: He can't be at home — all the lights are off.
commonMistakes.why: `Mustn't` nghĩa là 'không được phép', không dùng để suy đoán phủ định. Phủ định của `must` trong suy đoán là `can't`.

commonMistakes.wrong: May be the report is late.
commonMistakes.why: `Maybe` (một từ) là trạng từ 'có lẽ'. `May be` là modal + động từ, không đứng đầu câu theo cách này.

commonMistakes.wrong: It can be true, but I am not sure.
commonMistakes.right: It could be true, but I am not sure.
commonMistakes.why: `Can` diễn tả khả năng chung hoặc năng lực; khả năng xảy ra không chắc chắn dùng `could/may/might`.

commonMistakes.wrong: She might comes to the meeting.
commonMistakes.right: She might come to the meeting.
commonMistakes.why: Sau modal là động từ nguyên mẫu, không chia `-s`.

commonMistakes.wrong: He must have went home early.
commonMistakes.right: He must have gone home early.
commonMistakes.why: Sau `must have` phải là quá khứ phân từ (V3), không phải quá khứ đơn.

ieltsTips: Dùng `may`, `might`, `could` để hedge những khẳng định mạnh trong Task 2; điều này cải thiện cả Task Response lẫn Grammatical Range.
Tránh `mustn't` khi suy đoán phủ định; dùng `can't` để nói 'không thể nào'.
Trong Task 1, dùng `may` và `could` khi giải thích nguyên nhân có thể có của xu hướng, thay vì khẳng định chắc chắn khi biểu đồ không cho dữ liệu.
Trong Speaking Part 3, dùng `might` cho dự đoán xã hội (`People might become more isolated`) và `must` khi suy luận từ bằng chứng trước mắt.

exercises.question: The lights are off and the car is gone. He ___ at home.
exercises.explanation: Suy đoán phủ định chắc chắn dựa trên bằng chứng → **can't be**.

exercises.question: You've been travelling for twenty hours. You ___ exhausted.
exercises.explanation: Suy đoán khẳng định chắc chắn từ bằng chứng → **must be**.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses 'maybe' correctly?
options: May be the figures are wrong.
exercises.explanation: **Maybe** (một từ) = có lẽ, đứng đầu câu làm trạng từ.

exercises.question: If teachers were paid better, more graduates ___ the profession.
exercises.explanation: Trong tình huống giả định (unreal), dùng **might**, không dùng **may**.

exercises.question: Which sentence is the most appropriately hedged for Task 2?
options: Advertising may distort consumer choice in some cases.
exercises.explanation: **May ... in some cases** giảm nhẹ khẳng định, phù hợp văn phong học thuật.

exercises.question: The office is dark and the door is locked — everyone ___ (must / leave) already.
exercises.explanation: Suy đoán chắc chắn về quá khứ → **must have + V3**.

exercises.question: She ___ (can / not) have finished the thesis in one week — it is 200 pages long.
exercises.explanation: Suy đoán phủ định chắc chắn → **can't have + V3**.

exercises.question: The delay ___ (may / cause) by the new customs procedure.
exercises.hint: nguyên nhân có thể + bị động
exercises.explanation: Khả năng hiện tại dùng **may be + V3**; nếu sự việc đã xảy ra trong quá khứ thì **may have been caused**.

exercises.question: This approach ___ (could / reduce) costs by around 15%.
exercises.hint: khả năng có thể xảy ra
exercises.explanation: **Could + V** diễn tả khả năng được hedge, phù hợp Task 2.

exercises.question: The museum is closed today, so we ___ (might as well) come back tomorrow.
exercises.hint: không có lựa chọn nào tốt hơn
exercises.explanation: **Might as well + V** = không có cách nào tốt hơn.
